arxiv-1902-03199.title: Quantitative analysis of the interaction between a dc SQUID and an integrated micromechanical doubly clamped cantilever
arxiv-1902-03199.creator: Majdi Salman, Georgina M Klemencic, Soumen Mandal, Scott Manifold, Luqman Mustafa, Oliver A Williams, Sean R Giblin
arxiv-1902-03199.description: Abstract Based on the superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) equations described by the resistively- and capacitively-shunted junction model coupled to the equation of motion of a damped harmonic oscillator, we provide simulations to quantitatively describe the interaction between a dc SQUID and an integrated doubly clamped cantilever.

arxiv-2011-10379.title: Neural Scene Graphs for Dynamic Scenes
arxiv-2011-10379.creator: Julian Ost 1 Fahim Mannan 1 Nils Thürey 2 Julian Knodt 3 Felix Heide 1,3 1 Algolux 2 Technical University of Munich 3 Princeton University http://light.princeton.edu/neural-scene-graphs
arxiv-2011-10379.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Julian Ost 1 Fahim Mannan 1 Nils Thürey 2 Julian Knodt 3 Felix Heide 1,3 1 Algolux 2 Technical University of Munich 3 Princeton University http://light.princeton.edu/neural-scene-graphs. Recent implicit neural rendering methods have demonstrated that it is possible to learn accurate view synthesis for complex scenes by predicting their volumetric density and color supervised solely by a set of RGB images.

arxiv-2107-03050.title: Controlled Caption Generation for Images Through Adversarial Attacks
arxiv-2107-03050.creator: Nayyer Aafaq, Naveed Akhtar, Wei Liu, Mubarak Shah, Ajmal Mian
arxiv-2107-03050.description: Abstract Deep learning is found to be vulnerable to adversarial examples. However, its adversarial susceptibility in image caption generation is under-explored. We study adversarial examples for vision and language models, which typically adopt an encoder-decoder framework consisting of two major components: a Convolutional Neural Network ( i.e .

arxiv-2108-05932.title: Fundamental limits in Bayesian thermometry and attainability via adaptive strategies
arxiv-2108-05932.creator: Mohammad Mehboudi, Mathias R. Jørgensen, Stella Seah, Jonatan B. Brask, Jan Kołodyński, Martí Perarnau-Llobet
arxiv-2108-05932.description: Abstract We investigate the limits of thermometry using quantum probes at thermal equilibrium within the Bayesian approach. We consider the possibility of engineering interactions between the probes in order to enhance their sensitivity, as well as feedback during the measurement process, i.e., adaptive protocols.

arxiv-2108-08203.title: A compact instrument for gamma-ray burst detection on a CubeSat platform I
arxiv-2108-08203.creator: David Murphy, Alexey Ulyanov, Sheila McBreen, Maeve Doyle, Rachel Dunwoody, Joseph Mangan, Joseph Thompson, Brian Shortt, Antonio Martin-Carrillo, Lorraine Hanlon
arxiv-2108-08203.description: Abstract The Educational Irish Research Satellite 1 (EIRSAT-1) is a 2U CubeSat being developed under ESA’s Fly Your Satellite! programme. The project has many aspects, which are primarily educational, but also include space qualification of new detector technologies for gamma-ray astronomy and the detection of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs).

arxiv-2204-02497.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning via System Immersion and Random Matrix Encryption
arxiv-2204-02497.creator: Haleh Hayati, Carlos Murguia, Nathan van de Wouw
arxiv-2204-02497.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a privacy solution for collaborative distributed learning where clients train AI models directly on their devices instead of sharing their data with a centralized (potentially adversarial) server. Although FL preserves local data privacy to some extent, it has been shown that information about clients’ data can still be inferred from model updates.

arxiv-2208-14362.title: AutoWS-Bench-101: Benchmarking Automated Weak Supervision with 100 Labels
arxiv-2208-14362.creator: Nicholas Roberts, Xintong Li, Tzu-Heng Huang, Dyah Adila, Spencer Schoenberg, Cheng-Yu Liu, Lauren Pick, Haotian Ma, Aws Albarghouthi, Frederic Sala
arxiv-2208-14362.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nicholas Roberts, Xintong Li, Tzu-Heng Huang, Dyah Adila, Spencer Schoenberg, Cheng-Yu Liu, Lauren Pick, Haotian Ma, Aws Albarghouthi, Frederic Sala. Weak supervision (WS) is a powerful method to build labeled datasets for training supervised models in the face of little-to-no labeled data. It replaces hand-labeling data with aggregating multiple noisy-but-cheap label estimates expressed by labeling functions (LFs).

arxiv-2305-10087.title: Generating spectral dental panoramic images from single energy computed tomography volumes Journal: Physica Medica
arxiv-2305-10087.creator: Villseveri Somerkivi a,b,c , Anna Kolb a,b , Thorsten Sellerer a,b , Daniel Berthe a,b , York Hämisch d , Tuomas Pantsar d , Henrik Lohman d , Franz Pfeiffer a,b,e,f
arxiv-2305-10087.description: Abstract Purpose: To implement a framework generating synthetic spectral panoramic images from single energy CT volumes. Using the framework output to compare the synthetic images against experimental spectral panoramic images for cross-verification. Methods: A simulation framework for generating synthetic spectral panoramic images from CT volumes is described.

arxiv-2402-02035.title: Assessing Costs of Community Solar Integration via Optimal Distribution Grid Expansion
arxiv-2402-02035.creator: Miguel Heleno, Alan Valenzuela, Alexandre Moreira, Juan Pablo Carvallo
arxiv-2402-02035.description: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of distribution grid upgrades costs necessary to integrate Community Solar (CS) projects. The innovative methodology proposed for this quantification is based on incremental least-cost expansion of the distribution system, encompassing both traditional and non-traditional grid upgrade strategies.

arxiv-2404-15028.title: PRISM: A P romptable and R obust I nteractive S egmentation M odel with Visual Prompts
arxiv-2404-15028.creator: Hao Li, Han Liu, Dewei Hu, Jiacheng Wang, Ipek Oguz
arxiv-2404-15028.description: Abstract In this paper, we present PRISM, a P romptable and R obust I nteractive S egmentation M odel, aiming for precise segmentation of 3D medical images. PRISM accepts various visual inputs, including points, boxes, and scribbles as sparse prompts, as well as masks as dense prompts. Specifically, PRISM is designed with four principles to achieve robustness: (1) Iterative learning.

arxiv-2404-16520.title: Topological properties of finite-size heterostructures of magnetic topological insulators and superconductors
arxiv-2404-16520.creator: Julian Legendre, Eduárd Zsurka, Daniele Di Miceli, Llorenç Serra, Kristof Moors, Thomas L. Schmidt
arxiv-2404-16520.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Julian Legendre, Eduárd Zsurka, Daniele Di Miceli, Llorenç Serra, Kristof Moors, Thomas L. Schmidt. Heterostructures of magnetic topological insulators (MTIs) and superconductors (SCs) in two-dimensional (2D) slab and one-dimensional (1D) nanoribbon geometries have been predicted to host, respectively, chiral Majorana edge states (CMESs) and Majorana bound states (MBSs).

arxiv-2405-10101.title: Global analysis of the U ​ ( 3 ) 5 U(3)^{5} symmetric SMEFT
arxiv-2405-10101.creator: Riccardo Bartocci
arxiv-2405-10101.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Riccardo Bartocci. The U ​ ( 3 ) 5 U(3)^{5} symmetry within the SMEFT framework restricts the inclusion of only fully flavor-conserving operators at dimension six. This proceeding presents a global analysis of the SMEFT under this assumption. We provide global constraints on all 41 Wilson coefficients, utilizing leading-order and next-to-leading-order SMEFT predictions for various experiments including parity-violating experiments, Electroweak Precision Observables (EWPO), Higgs physics, top quark interactions, flavor observables, dijet production, and lepton scatterings.

arxiv-2405-19528.title: Predicting Long-Term Human Behaviors in Discrete Representations via Physics-Guided Diffusion
arxiv-2405-19528.creator: Zhitian Zhang, Anjian Li, Angelica Lim, Mo Chen
arxiv-2405-19528.description: Abstract Long-term human trajectory prediction is a challenging yet critical task in robotics and autonomous systems. Prior work that studied how to predict accurate short-term human trajectories with only unimodal features often failed in long-term prediction. Reinforcement learning provides a good solution for learning human long-term behaviors but can suffer from challenges in data efficiency and optimization.

arxiv-2407-01156.title: Influence of a squeezed prewell on tunneling properties and bound states in heterostructures
arxiv-2407-01156.creator: Yaroslav Zolotaryuk and Alexander V. Zolotaryuk
arxiv-2407-01156.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yaroslav Zolotaryuk and Alexander V. Zolotaryuk. A resonant tunneling effect of an extremely thin potential well on the transmission of charged particles through a planar heterostructure with an arbitrary potential profile is investigated in a squeezing limit as the well width tends to zero. In this limit, the transmission probability through the structure is shown to be blocked for all the parameter values of the well, except a resonance set of Lebesgue measure zero.

arxiv-2408-03269.title: Connections Beyond Data: Exploring Homophily With Visualizations
arxiv-2408-03269.creator: Poorna Talkad Sukumar Maurizio Porfiri Oded Nov New York University
arxiv-2408-03269.description: Abstract Homophily refers to the tendency of individuals to associate with others who are similar to them in characteristics, such as, race, ethnicity, age, gender, or interests. In this paper, we investigate if individuals exhibit racial homophily when viewing visualizations, using mass shooting data in the United States as the example topic.

arxiv-2412-02810.title: Universal Rates of Empirical Risk Minimization
arxiv-2412-02810.creator: Steve Hanneke, Mingyue Xu
arxiv-2412-02810.description: Abstract The well-known empirical risk minimization (ERM) principle is the basis of many widely used machine learning algorithms, and plays an essential role in the classical PAC theory. A common description of a learning algorithm’s performance is its so-called “learning curve”, that is, the decay of the expected error as a function of the input sample size.

arxiv-2506-05277.title: On Minimizers of Minimum Density
arxiv-2506-05277.creator: Arseny Shur
arxiv-2506-05277.description: Abstract Minimizers are sampling schemes with numerous applications in computational biology. Assuming a fixed alphabet of size σ \sigma , a minimizer is defined by two integers k , w ≥ 2 k,w\geq 2 and a linear order ρ \rho on strings of length k k (also called k k -mers).

arxiv-2507-05377.title: Engineering giant transmon molecules as mediators of conditional two-photon gates
arxiv-2507-05377.creator: Tomás Levy-Yeyati, Tomás Ramos, Alejandro González-Tudela
arxiv-2507-05377.description: Abstract Artificial atoms non-locally coupled to waveguides – the so-called giant atoms– offer new opportunities for the control of light and matter. In this work, we show how to use an array of non-locally coupled transmon “molecules” to engineer a passive photonic controlled gate for waveguide photons.

arxiv-2601-13450.title: Four Cold Super-Jupiters Revealed by Extended and Complex Microlensing Signals
arxiv-2601-13450.creator: Cheongho Han, Chung-Uk Lee, Michael D. Albrow, Sun-Ju Chung, Andrew Gould, Youn Kil Jung, Kyu-Ha Hwang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu, Yossi Shvartzvald, In-Gu Shin, Jennifer C. Yee, Weicheng Zang, Hongjing Yang, Doeon Kim, Dong-Jin Kim, Sang-Mok Cha, Seung-Lee Kim, Dong-Joo Lee, Yongseok Lee, Byeong-Gon Park, Rich
arxiv-2601-13450.description: Abstract We present the analysis of four microlensing events, KMT-2020-BLG-0202, KMT-2022-BLG-1551, KMT-2023-BLG-0466, and KMT-2025-BLG-0121, which exhibit extended and complex anomalies in their light curves. These events were identified through a systematic reanalysis of KMTNet data aimed at detecting planetary signals that deviate from the typical short-term anomaly morphology.

arxiv-2602-24132.title: Isospin breaking corrections to the hadronic vacuum polarization with stochastic coordinate sampling
arxiv-2602-24132.creator: J. Tobias Tsang
arxiv-2602-24132.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by J. Tobias Tsang. In the recent Muon g-2 Theory Initiative white paper update, the hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution – which dominates the theoretical uncertainty – is evaluated as an average of different lattice QCD calculations. Since lattice simulations are mostly carried out in isospin symmetric QCD, corrections due to the mass difference of the up and down quarks and the coupling to photons have to be accounted for.

arxiv-2605-22454.creator: Benjamin Poole bpoole16@charlotte.edu, Andrew Quinn aquinn16@charlotte.edu, Li Yang lyang50@charlotte.edu, Minwoo Lee minwoo.lee@charlotte.edu

arxiv-2606-29438.creator: Yuecai Han hanyc@jlu.edu.cn, Jianming Xu xujm24@mails.jlu.edu.cn

plos-pone-0005766.title: Structure of Human DNA Polymerase κ Inserting dATP Opposite an 8-OxoG DNA Lesion
plos-pone-0005766.creator: Rodrigo Vasquez-Del Carpio, Timothy D. Silverstein, Samer Lone et al.
plos-pone-0005766.description: PLOS ONE research article. Oxygen-free radicals formed during normal aerobic cellular metabolism attack bases in DNA and 7,8-dihydro-8-oxoguanine (8-oxoG) is one of the major lesions formed. It is amongst the most mutagenic lesions in cells because of its dual coding potential, wherein 8-oxoG( syn ) can pa

pmc-10544490.title: A neuromusculoskeletal modelling approach to bilateral hip mechanics due to unexpected lateral perturbations during overground walking
pmc-10544490.creator: Yunchao Zhu, Ji Huang, Xin Ma, Wen-Ming Chen
pmc-10544490.description: BackgroundCurrent studies on how external perturbations impact gait dynamics have primarily focused on the changes in the body's center of mass (CoM) during treadmill walking. The biomechanical responses, in particular to the multi-planar hip joint coordination, following perturbations in overground walking conditions are not completely known.

pmc-10548537.title: Viable Clostridium botulinum spores not detected in the household dust of major Canadian cities
pmc-10548537.creator: Richard A. Harris, Madeleine Blondin-Brosseau, Christine Levesque, Pat E. Rasmussen, Suzanne Beauchemin, John W. Austin
pmc-10548537.description: Clostridium botulinum causes infant botulism by colonising the intestines and producing botulinum neurotoxin in situ. Previous reports have linked infant botulism cases to C. botulinum spores in household dust, yet the baseline incidence of C. botulinum spores in residential households is currently unknown. Vacuum cleaner dust from 963 households in 13 major Canadian cities was tested for C.

pmc-10613297.title: A novel neural-evolutionary framework for predicting weight on the bit in drilling operations
pmc-10613297.creator: Masrour Dowlatabadi, Saeed Azizi, Mohsen Dehbashi, Hamed Sadeqi
pmc-10613297.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study compares the performance of artificial neural networks (ANN) trained by grey wolf optimization (GWO), biogeography-based optimization (BBO), and Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) to estimate the weight on bit (WOB). To this end, a dataset consisting of drilling depth, drill string rotational speed, rate of penetration, and volumetric flow rate as input variables and the WOB as a response is used to develop and validate the intelligent tools.

pmc-10834744.title: Multi-omics approaches to studying gastrointestinal microbiome in the context of precision medicine and machine learning
pmc-10834744.creator: Jingyue Wu, Stephanie S. Singleton, Urnisha Bhuiyan, Lori Krammer, Raja Mazumder
pmc-10834744.description: The human gastrointestinal (gut) microbiome plays a critical role in maintaining host health and has been increasingly recognized as an important factor in precision medicine. High-throughput sequencing technologies have revolutionized -omics data generation, facilitating the characterization of the human gut microbiome with exceptional resolution.

pmc-11426193.title: Surgical Outcomes of a Human Umbilical Cord Allograft Over the Ahmed Glaucoma Valve Plate for Refractory Glaucoma
pmc-11426193.creator: Aparna Rao
pmc-11426193.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives: To report the surgical outcomes of sterile dehydrated human umbilical cord allograft over the Ahmed glaucoma valve (AGV) plate for refractory glaucoma.Methods: Thirty-four eyes of 34 patients with refractory glaucoma who underwent AGV with umbilical cord allograft (AmnioPlast THICK™; Life Cell International Private Limited, Mumbai, India) placed over the AGV plate between September 2021 and 2022 at a tertiary eye care centre were included (group1) and compared with 30 eyes of 30 patients undergoing AGV without amnioblasts (group 2).

pmc-12730127.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Spectator Viewing Behavior in Sports Events: Mediating Role of Viewing Motivation and Moderating Role of Player Identification
pmc-12730127.creator: Jie Min, Qing Xie, Yongjian Liu, John Parkinson, Ekta Sinha, Jalal Sarabadani
pmc-12730127.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). With the widespread application of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the sports industry, the spectator’s experience is increasingly shaped by AI-driven features. To explore the mechanism through which the perceived AI-enabled spectating experience affects viewing behavior, and to validate the mediating role of viewing motivation (SDT Needs Satisfaction) in the relationship between AI and viewing behavior as well as the moderating role of player identification in this mediating pathway, we adopted literature review, survey, and empirical analysis methods.

pmc-13195796.title: Uncommon Occurrence of Compound Nevus in the Oral Cavity
pmc-13195796.creator: Akash Nhemaphuki, Manoj Humagain, Arjun Hari Rijal, Simant Lamichhane, Sachita Thapa, Sujan Timsina, Tommaso Lombardi
pmc-13195796.description: IntroductionCompound nevi are less common. Compound nevi account for approximately 5.9%–16.5% of all reported oral melanocytic nevi. Current evidence suggests no clear association with patient age or sex. The oral compound nevus is most typically found on the hard palate and buccal mucosa, with fewer cases occurring elsewhere in the mouth.

pmc-13386097.title: Genotype-immunophenotype relationships in NPM1-mutated AML clonal evolution uncovered by single-cell multiomic analysis∗
pmc-13386097.creator: Morgan Drucker, Darren Lee, Michael Bowman, Xuan Zhang, Bailee N Kain, Deedra Nicolet, Roopsha Bandopadhyay, Varsha Singh, Zhe Wang, Richard M Stone, Caner Saygin, Krzysztof Mrózek, Andrew J Carroll, Daniel T Starczynowski, Ross L Levine, John C Byrd, Nathan Salomonis, Sarah J Skuli, H Leighton Grim
pmc-13386097.description: Key Points•In NPM1-mutated AML, comutations in epigenetic modifier genes can dictate unique lineage trajectories in subsequent clones.•Signaling gene comutations in NPM1-mutated AML at relapse are correlated with increased clonal diversity and shortened overall survival. Introduction Nucleophosmin 1 (NPM1) mutations1,2 are found in ∼30% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML)3,4 who also harbor epigenetic and signaling gene mutations.

pmc-13547399.title: Identification of a membrane transporter for dimethylsulfoniopropionate uptake in marine eukaryotic phytoplankton
pmc-13547399.creator: Rafel Simó, Jean-François Mangot, Valerie Vergé, Jean-Claude Lozano, Violeta Saló, Clara Ruiz-González, Daffne López-Sandoval, Yaiza M Castillo, Ronald P Kiene, Stephen D Archer, François-Yves Bouget, José M González
pmc-13547399.description: Marine microalgae obtain essential sulfur through energetically costly, assimilatory reduction of sea-salt sulfate, so the ability for osmotrophic incorporation of reduced sulfur would confer them adaptability in energy-limiting conditions. Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a common marine osmolyte whose pervasive occurrence in seawater makes it as good a candidate for supplying reduced sulfur to marine eukaryotes as it is to prokaryotes.

pmc-5642006.title: A review of instrumental variable estimators for Mendelian randomization
pmc-5642006.creator: Burgess S, Small DS, Thompson SG.
pmc-5642006.description: Peer-reviewed research article (PubMed Central). Instrumental variable analysis is an approach for obtaining causal inferences on the effect of an exposure (risk factor) on an outcome from observational data. It has gained in popularity over the past decade with the use of genetic variants as instrumental variables, known as Me
